name: Standard (red tail, goose roundel)
description: All-white fuselage with 'TURKISH AIRLINES' in heavy dark-blue capitals above the forward windows; a large pale-gray goose watermark on the rear fuselage behind the wing; red fin with the white-ringed red roundel and white goose low and aft on it; red winglets carrying a small roundel; white engines.

logos.description: A white ring round a red disc holding a white stylised wild goose: a crescent wing whose convex edge faces forward on the left side, a short spike pointing forward from its foot and a long pointed tail running down and aft to the ring; set low on the fin, its aft edge almost touching the trailing edge. Same artwork on both sides (not mirrored).
The goose alone, very large, as a pale-gray outline watermark on the rear fuselage behind the wing, over and below the window line.
Small white roundel with the red goose near the top of each winglet's outer face.

titles.style: Heavy, slightly wide sans capitals in dark blue, above the windows from just aft of the forward door. Re-measured 2026-11-15: starts just aft of the forward door's frame, its baseline a hair above the window tops, cap height about 0.65 m.

notes: Each aircraft also carries a city name in small dark capitals under the cockpit (e.g. 'NEVŞEHİR') and a small star by the cockpit; not drawn. The belly wasn't seen squarely; photos from below-front show it white. Wide-bodies (A330, A350, 777, 787) carry the same scheme at their own proportions. When this scheme was introduced isn't sourced here (around 2010, unverified), so `from` is left out.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (a few colors from memory) with the current scheme drawn from dated Commons photos.
